summary: This page provides a troubleshooting guide for TIG/Stick welding problems, their possible causes, and likely solutions for the Vulcan OmniPro 220 welder.
text_content:
Troubleshooting–TIG/Stick Welding

IMPORTANT!
Be CERTAIN to shut off the Welder, disconnect it from power, and discharge the electrode to ground before adjusting, cleaning, or repairing the unit.

Problem | Possible Causes | Likely Solutions

Welder Does Not Function When Switched On
1. Tripped thermal protection device. | 1. Reduce duration or frequency of welding periods to help reduce wear on the welder. Refer to Duty Cycle (Duration of Use) on page 29.
2. Faulty or improperly connected Trigger. | 2. Qualified technician must check and secure/replace Trigger.
3. Ground Clamp not attached to workpiece. | 3. Attach Ground Clamp to workpiece.
4. Shielding Gas not connected. | 4. Connect shielding gas to Welder.

LCD Display Does Not Light When Welder is Switched On
1. Unit is not connected to outlet properly. | 1. Verify the voltage at the outlet and the connection to the outlet.
2. Outlet is unpowered. | 2. Check circuit breaker/GFCI devices; if any are tripped, determine and remedy cause before resetting. Verify that the circuit is designed to supply the required input amperage as detailed in Specifications on page 7.

Weak Arc Strength
1. Incorrect line voltage. | 1. Check the line voltage and, if insufficient, have a licensed electrician remedy the situation.
2. Improper gauge or length of cord. | 2. Do not use an extension cord on this Welder. Use only one of the supplied power cords for this Welder or an identical replacement cord.

Welding Arc Not Stable.
1. Loose electrode cable or ground cable. | 1. Check to ensure that all connections are tight.
2. Damaged electrode holder or loose connection within electrode holder. | 2. Have a qualified technician inspect and repair/replace as necessary.
3. Adjust current setting. | 3. Make sure setting matches recommended setting on chart.
4. Shielding gas getting low. | 4. Replace shielding gas cylinder.

Follow all safety precautions whenever diagnosing or servicing the equipment.

key_facts: Before adjusting, cleaning, or repairing the unit, shut off the Welder, disconnect it from power, and discharge the electrode to ground
Tripped thermal protection device can cause welder to not function when switched on
Reducing duration or frequency of welding periods helps reduce wear on the welder
Duty Cycle (Duration of Use) information is on page 29
A faulty or improperly connected Trigger requires a qualified technician to check and secure/replace
Ground Clamp must be attached to workpiece for welder to function
Shielding gas must be connected for welder to function in TIG/Stick mode
LCD display not lighting can be caused by unit not connected to outlet properly or outlet being unpowered
Check circuit breaker/GFCI devices if LCD display does not light
Specifications including required input amperage are on page 7
Weak arc strength can be caused by incorrect line voltage or improper gauge or length of cord
Do not use an extension cord on this Welder
Only use supplied power cords or identical replacement cords for this Welder
Unstable welding arc can be caused by loose electrode cable or ground cable, damaged electrode holder, incorrect current setting, or low shielding gas
Replace shielding gas cylinder if shielding gas is getting low
A qualified technician should inspect and repair/replace a damaged electrode holder
